Find the total area $A$ of the region between the curve $y={x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=4,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(x-3) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Since $3\in [1,4],$ we have two regions: 

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=1$ to $x=3.$

- The area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x=3$ to $x=4.$

Notice that the region for $x\in [1,3]$ lies completely below the $x$-axis. Hence, the value of

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{3}({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x
$$

will be negative. Therefore, the area that we want is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =-{\int }_{1}^{3}({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+3{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}\,{|}_{1}^{3}+{x}^{3}\,{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}[{3}^{4}-{1}^{4}]+[{3}^{3}-{1}^{3}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}[81-1]+[27-1] \\  & =-20+26 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x\in [3,4],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & ={\int }_{3}^{4}({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}\,{|}_{3}^{4}-{x}^{3}\,{|}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{4}^{4}-{3}^{4}]-[{4}^{3}-{3}^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[256-81]-[64-27] \\  & =\frac{175}{4}-37 \\  & =\frac{27}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the total area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =6+\frac{27}{4} \\  & =\frac{24}{4}+\frac{27}{4} \\  & =\frac{51}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
